missing: Confirm that the invariant is intended to apply when finalizing a slash, rather than only when requesting one; the design rationale leaves this uncertain.
Demonstrate that finalizing the queued slash after unstaking actually reduces the operator’s vault balance or otherwise causes loss; the PoC only shows that the call does not revert.
reason: The cited code supports the sequence and does not re-check registration at slash finalization. But the report does not establish that the intended invariant applies at that point or demonstrate a resulting loss, so the claimed impact is not yet supported.

evidence.claim: A DSS can finalize a queued slashing after the operator has unstaked its vaults and unregistered from that DSS, violating the invariant that only DSSs an operator is registered with can slash it.
evidence.support_reason: finalizeSlashing (SlasherLib.sol:126-151) only checks the stored slash root and veto window; it never re-checks operator registration or that the vault is still staked to the DSS. unregisterOperatorFromDSS (Operator.sol:181-203) only requires vaultStakedInDssMap to be empty, which finalizeUpdateVaultStakeInDSS clears (Operator.sol:103-109) without regard to pending slashings. So the sequence requestSlashing -> unstake finalize -> unregister -> finalizeSlashing succeeds.
preconditions: Operator has a queued unstake for all vaults staked to the DSS and the MIN_STAKE_UPDATE_DELAY has passed
DSS has a queued slashing within the veto window on those vaults
Operator finalizes unstake and unregisters before the veto window expires
missing_evidence: Confirmation that the invariant 'only DSSs an operator is registered with can slash' is intended to hold at finalization time, not just at request time (the README lists it as a main invariant, but the design comment at Vault.sol:154 and the withdrawal-delay rationale suggest slashing of already-queued operations is intended)
Demonstration that the slashed amount is actually taken from the operator's vault after unstaking (the PoC only asserts the call does not revert)
